# Disagreement Log — Apocalypse of Peter, Chapter 15
**Agents:** EMET | LOGOS | PNEUMA
**Total Disagreements:** 10

---

## Verse-by-Verse Disagreements

### v.1 — "want to see" vs. "wish to see" vs. "I want to see"
- **EMET:** "I want to see"
- **LOGOS:** "I wish to see"
- **PNEUMA:** "I want to see"
- **Note:** Minor. "Wish" is slightly more formal; both acceptable.

### v.1 — "who had not sinned" vs. "who never sinned"
- **EMET/LOGOS:** "who had not sinned"
- **PNEUMA:** "who never sinned"
- **Note:** "Never sinned" (PNEUMA) implies sinlessness by nature; "had not sinned" implies they successfully avoided sin. Minor but real distinction.

### v.4 — "light that was from their faces" vs. "light that came from them"
- **EMET:** "light that was from their faces"
- **LOGOS:** "light that came from their faces"
- **PNEUMA:** "light from their faces was too great"
- **Note:** PNEUMA adds "too great" — an intensifier not in source.

### v.4 — "I cannot describe it" positioning
- **EMET:** Placed after "clothing was shining"
- **LOGOS:** "with a light I cannot describe"
- **PNEUMA:** "a radiance I have no language for"
- **Note:** PNEUMA's "I have no language for" is more dramatic; "I cannot describe" (EMET/LOGOS) is the literal rendering.

### v.5 — "these are your brothers the righteous" vs. "these are your righteous brothers"
- **EMET:** "these are your brothers the righteous"
- **LOGOS/PNEUMA:** "these are your righteous brothers"
- **Note:** Minor word-order difference. "Your brothers the righteous" (EMET) preserves a more formal appositive structure.

### v.6 — "where has the flesh gone from them" vs. "where is their flesh"
- **EMET:** "where has the flesh gone from them"
- **LOGOS/PNEUMA:** "where is their flesh"
- **Note:** LOGOS/PNEUMA simplify. EMET's "gone from them" preserves the departing aspect.

### v.7 — A problematic verse
- **EMET:** "I will show you also what I have shown to you before this. Go and bring it that I may see."
- **LOGOS:** "I will show you what I showed you before. Go and bring it, that I may see."
- **PNEUMA:** "I will show you what I showed you once before. Come — bring it, that I may see."
- **Note:** The verse is obscure in all witnesses. The referent of "bring it" is unclear. All agents preserve the obscurity; PNEUMA's "Come" is an addition.

### v.8 — "wonderful" vs. "indescribable" (PNEUMA)
- **EMET:** "raiment was wonderful"
- **LOGOS:** "garments wonderful beyond description"
- **PNEUMA:** "garments were extraordinary — indescribable"
- **Note:** LOGOS's "beyond description" and PNEUMA's "indescribable" are both additions to the source's simple "wonderful." SOPHIA prefers LOGOS's moderating phrase.

### v.9 — "voice of the lightning of thunder" vs. "voice like lightning and thunder"
- **EMET:** "as the voice of the lightning of thunder"
- **LOGOS/PNEUMA:** "like the voice of lightning and thunder"
- **Note:** EMET's "lightning of thunder" preserves the genitive chain; "lightning and thunder" (LOGOS) is cleaner and conventional.

### v.12 — "the shape of the Lord" vs. "the form of the Lord"
- **EMET:** "the shape of the Lord"
- **LOGOS:** "the form of the Lord"
- **PNEUMA:** "the form of the Lord"
- **Note:** "Form" (*morphē*) is theologically preferred; "shape" is adequate but misses the Pauline resonance.

---
*10 disagreements. SOPHIA: "form" not "shape" (v.12); "lightning and thunder" (v.9); "had not sinned" (v.1); "I cannot describe" (v.4).*
